description: Corrections found by checking contests against a named source. Each record names the imported file, the source that shows the right figures, and why. The raw file stays as imported; scripts/build-test2-election-manifest.mjs (applySourceCheckedFixes) lays the operations over it at build time and shows the reason in the contest's 'Corrected' note. Operations: set {path, value}; candidate {name, set}; addCandidate {row}; replaceCandidates {candidates}.

batches.ni-and-dail-2026-10-18: Northern Ireland local government 1973-2011, the 1996 Forum (Belfast East) and two 2014 Dáil by-elections, checked against ARK Northern Ireland Elections, Wikipedia and ElectionsIreland.org.
batches.roi-local-2026-10-18: Irish local elections checked against IrelandElection.com (the independent check) and ElectionsIreland.org (the site Civgraph's figures were first taken from): winners not marked as elected, seat counts, quotas, and contests imported with no candidates or no votes, filled only where every candidate has a first preference that adds up to the page's valid poll and the winners equal the seats. Fills for 1974, 1979 and 1985 apply when those years are published.
batches.dail-byelections-2026-10-18: Dáil by-elections 2009-2021 imported with second-count figures as first preferences, missing candidates or a stray row, checked against ElectionsIreland.org and Wikipedia.
batches.official-records-2026-10-23: Results contradicted by official membership records: Dáil winners and Ceann Comhairle automatic returns (Houses of the Oireachtas, with ElectionsIreland.org and Wikipedia), NI Assembly and Westminster winners (NI Assembly, UK Parliament), and 2014 and 2019 council candidates the import left named 'Party' (ARK Northern Ireland Elections, Democracy Club, CC BY 4.0).
batches.eoni-2014-2026-10-26: Northern Ireland local council election of 22 May 2014, every contest checked candidate by candidate and stage by stage against the Electoral Office for Northern Ireland's result sheets as published on Open Data NI (Open Government Licence).
batches.eoni-wayback-2026-10-26: Northern Ireland council contests checked against the Electoral Office for Northern Ireland's own result sheets and results booklets, retrieved from the Internet Archive's copies of eoni.org.uk. Figures from the scanned booklets were read from the page images, not taken from OCR, and confirmed by the site owner.
batches.ni-council-xref-2026-10-27: Northern Ireland council contests 1973-2011 cross-checked against ARK's per-contest result spreadsheets (Nicholas Whyte, ark.ac.uk), the Wikipedia council election articles and the quota each result sheet states (the valid poll divided by one more than the seats, rounded down, plus one).
batches.person-id-splits-2026-10-28: Candidates of the same name in different councils that the imported data gave one Candidate_Id, and so one person record. Each council's candidate is given an id of their own; within a council they stay together until a source says otherwise.
batches.candidate-id-splits-2026-10-28: The imported Northern Ireland council data gave every candidate of one name the same Candidate_Id in every council, joining different people into one. Each such id keeps the council where it is used most; elsewhere each council's candidate gets an id of their own ('<id>-<council>'). Nothing in the results changes.
batches.gallagher-1923-first-prefs-2026-10-28: First-preference figures for the August 1923 Dail election taken from Michael Gallagher, Irish Elections 1922-44: Results and Analysis (1993), where the imported figures did not add up to the valid poll.
batches.gallagher-1922-44-counts-2026-10-29: Count tables for 1922-44 Dail contests taken from Michael Gallagher, Irish Elections 1922-44: Results and Analysis (1993), where the imported data had none or only first preferences (count sidecars in data/elections/dail-wikipedia-counts named as Gallagher's), with the figures and names his tables show to be wrong in the imported data corrected. Figures read from the page images.
batches.ni-dea-names-2026-10-29: Northern Ireland council contests 1973-2011 in Newry and Mourne, North Down, Newtownabbey (1985), Coleraine and Limavady (1989) that were shown under their import spreadsheet names, named as ARK Northern Ireland Elections and the electoral-area maps name them.
batches.party-labels-2026-10-29: Party labels corrected: Dail candidates of June 1927 (National League), 1943-44 (Clann na Talmhan) and 1944-48 (National Labour) shown as Independents, checked against Gallagher's Irish Elections 1922-44, Wikipedia and the Houses of the Oireachtas; Michael Sheehan (Cork Borough 1948) and Thomas O'Hara (Mayo North 1951-57) shown as Fine Gael; and two Unionist Party of Northern Ireland candidates of October 1974 shown as Ulster Unionists, from the nomination notice.
batches.ark-crosscheck-2026-10-29: Disagreements between ARK Northern Ireland Elections (Nicholas Whyte) and Civgraph settled against the Electoral Office for Northern Ireland's result sheets and results booklets (Internet Archive copies).
